title: Two British tourists among four killed in fatal cable-car crash near Naples, Italy
summary: Two British tourists and two others died after a traction cable snapped on a cable car near Monte Faito in Castellammare di Stabia, Italy, on April 17. Prosecutors have opened an investigation into multiple manslaughter and culpable disaster. A fifth person was seriously injured, several passengers were evacuated, and local officials declared a day of mourning as rescuers and investigators work at the scene.
content:
Two British tourists and an Israeli national were among four people who died in a cable car crash on Thursday, April 17, near Monte Faito in the town of Castellammare di Stabia, close to Naples, Italy.

Italian prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into the accident relating to the cable car that connects the seaside town of Castellammare di Stabia to Mount Faito. Initial reports indicate that a traction cable snapped, bringing cable cars to a halt.

A fifth person, believed to be a foreign tourist, was seriously injured during the incident, and a number of people had to be evacuated from another cable car. Emergency services including firefighters, police and Italy's alpine rescue units were dispatched to the scene.

Authorities said an investigation has been opened into possible multiple manslaughter and culpable disaster. Checks are being carried out on the cable car system and investigators are examining whether strong winds might have been a contributing factor.

Vincenzo De Luca, president of the Campania region, described the day as "truly tragic and painful," saying his thoughts are with those who died, the injured and their families. He thanked rescuers and said an inquiry into what happened would be carried out.

Luigi Vicinanza, mayor of Castellammare, said he had declared a day of mourning and cancelled Easter holiday initiatives. He added that a minute's silence would be held on Friday in memory of those who died.

The crash occurred on a stretch of line between the popular tourist areas of Pompeii and Sorrento. EAV, the public transport firm that runs the cable car, said the service had reopened a week earlier and that it had met required safety conditions before reopening.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni offered condolences from Washington DC, where she was meeting with US President Donald Trump.

An eyewitness account from a British tourist, Megan Pacey, 50, of London, described seeing people winched down in a harness from one cable car following the incident. Ms Pacey, who was with her husband and two children, said: "We were within a minute or two of the incident happening. They started winching people down from the cable car. We watched the first couple of people come down in a harness and as we left, there was a sense of urgency that had kicked in."

She also reported seeing flowers and candles on the steps outside the local railway station, and that emergency services remained at the scene.

A Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office spokesperson said the UK was "dealing with an incident in Italy and are in contact with the local authorities," adding that their thoughts are with those affected and that staff are available 24/7 to support British nationals abroad.

content.title: Two British tourists dead after fatal cable car crash kills four people in Italy
content.content:
Two British tourists and an Israeli national were among four people who died in a cable car crash on Thursday(Image: PA)

Two British tourists have died in a tragic cable car crash near Naples, Italy, that took place on Thursday, April 17.

Italian news agency Ansa has reported that two British tourists and an Israeli national were among the four people who died in the crash on Thursday, April 17, at Monte Faito in the town of Castellammare di Stabia, reportedly revealed by Naples mayor Gaetano Manfredi.

Ansa has reported that prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into accident relating to the cable-car which connects the seaside town of Castellamare di Stabia to Mount Faito.

A traction cable snapped bringing cable cars to a halt, according to initial information. A fifth person, believed to be a foreign tourist, was seriously injured during the incident, and a number of people had to be evacuated from another cable car.

An investigation into multiple manslaughter and culpable disaster has been opened by Italian prosecutors, according to reports.

In a translated post on social media, Vincenzo De Luca, president of Campania, called the day “truly tragic and painful” and said his thoughts go to those who died, were injured and their families. He said he was grateful for the rescuers and said an investigation into what happened will be carried out.

Luigi Vicinanza Sindaco, the mayor of Castellammare, said on Facebook that there will be a day of mourning and decided to cancel all initiatives for theEasterholidays. He added that a minute’s silence would be held on Friday in memory of those who died.

Firefighters, police and Italy’s alpine rescue were sent to the scene, which is between the popular tourist areas of Pompeii and Sorrento.

EAV public transport firm, which runs the cable car, said the service had reopened a week ago with all the required safety conditions.

Checks were being carried out by investigators on the cable car and the possibility that strong wind was among the causes of the incident.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her condolences from Washington DC, where she met with US President Donald Trump.

A British tourist said she saw people being evacuated in a harness from one cable car following the incident.

Megan Pacey, 50, from London, was with her husband, James Ross, and their two children Hannah, 10, and eight-year-old son, Luke, when they saw a suspended cable car.

She said: “We were within a minute or two of (the incident) happening.

“They started winching people down from the cable car. We watched the first couple of people come down in a harness and as we left, there was a sense of urgency that had kicked in.”

She said she saw flowers and candles on the steps outside the railway station on Friday and emergency services remained at the scene.

A Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office spokesperson said: “We are dealing with an incident in Italy and are in contact with the local authorities. Our thoughts are with those affected.

“Our staff are available 24/7 to support British nationals abroad.”
